en: I worship the state of Rāmacandra, which is to be known through the Sāvitrī Upaniṣad, radiant with the word "Savitṛ" (the Illuminator), and entirely free from all counter-correlates. || 1 ||
The Sāvitrī, the Pāśupata, the Supreme Brahman, the Avadhūtaka;
the Tripurātapana, the Goddess, the Tripurā, and the Kaṭhabhāvanā. || 2 ||

Oṃ! May my limbs, speech, breath, sight, hearing, as well as strength and all my senses, swell with vigor. May everything be the Upaniṣad of Brahman. May I not repudiate Brahman; may Brahman not repudiate me. May there be no repudiation; may there be non-repudiation.
May they be mine! Whatever dharmas are contained in the Upanishads for one intent upon the Self—may those be in me; may they be in me!
Who is Savitṛ? Who is Sāvitrī? Agni indeed is Savitṛ, and the Earth is Sāvitrī.
Where Agni is, there is the Earth; and where the Earth is, there is Agni. These two are the two wombs; that is one couple. ||1||
Who is Savitṛ? Who is Sāvitrī? Varuṇa indeed is Savitṛ, and the waters are Sāvitrī.
Wherever Varuṇa is, there are the waters; and wherever the waters are, there is Varuṇa. These two are a womb; that is one couple. ||~2||
Who is Savitṛ? Who is Sāvitrī? Vāyu alone is Savitṛ, and Ākāśa is Sāvitrī.
Where there is Vāyu, there is Ākāśa; and where there is Ākāśa, there is Vāyu. These two are the two wombs; that is one couple. ||3||
Who is Savitṛ? What is Sāvitrī? The sacrifice itself is Savitṛ; the meters (candāṃsi) are Sāvitrī.
Where there is the sacrifice, there are the meters; or where there are the meters, that is the sacrifice. These two are the womb; that is one couple. || 4 ||
Who is Savitṛ? Who is Sāvitrī? The thunder is indeed Savitṛ, and the lightning is Sāvitrī.
Where there is thunder, there is lightning; and where there is lightning, there is thunder. These two have a common womb; that is one couple. || 5 ||
Who is Savitṛ? Who is Sāvitrī? Āditya indeed is Savitṛ, and the sky is Sāvitrī.
Wherever Āditya is, there is the sky; or wherever the sky is, there is Āditya. These two are the womb, and that is one couple. || 6 ||
Who is Savitṛ? Who is Sāvitrī? The moon alone is Savitṛ, and the stars are Sāvitrī.
Wherever the moon is, there are the stars; or wherever the stars are, there is the moon. These two are the womb; that is one couple. || 7 ||

Who is Savitṛ? What is Sāvitrī? Mind alone is Savitṛ; speech is Sāvitrī. Wherever there is mind, there is speech; wherever there is speech, there is mind. These two have a single source; that is one couple. || 8 ||
Who is Savitṛ? Who is Sāvitrī? Man indeed is Savitṛ; woman is Sāvitrī. Where there is man, there is woman;
or where there is woman, there is man. These two are the womb; that is one couple. 9.

The first quarter of that very [verse] is "bhūs tat savitur vareṇyam"; Agni is indeed the desirable, the waters are the desirable, and the moon is the desirable. The second quarter of that very [verse] is "bhargo devasya dhīmahi"; Agni is indeed *bhargas*.
The sun is indeed *bhargas*, the moon is indeed *bhargas*. Of that [Sāvitrī], this is the third quarter: "May he who impels us from heaven. Both woman and man procreate;
and whoever knows this Sāvitrī thus, he [escapes] rebirth.
Victory to the Supreme Puruṣa, the sovereign of Bala and Atibala! Gāyatrī is the meter;
Gāyatrī is the deity; the syllables *a*, *u*, and *m* are the seed-syllables and others;
the application is for the removal of hunger and other afflictions; *klāṃ* and so forth is the ritual placement of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*).

To those two who are moistened by the palm of the hand of immortality, who are richly endowed with the power to revive all beings and are highly skilled in removing calamities; who are rays within the essence of the Vedas; who are transformations consisting of the *praṇava*; whose bodies have the form of the sun; and who are eternally unborn—[to them, I bow].
Balā and atibalā at the end.
Oṃ hrīṃ! O powerful Mahādevī, hrīṃ! O you of great power, klīṃ! O bestower of the attainment of the fourfold aims of human life, O you whose essence is the granting of boons to that Savitṛ!
Hrīṃ! O you whose essence is the granting of boons, [bestow] the most excellent splendor of the divine! O Atibale, O you whose form is universal compassion!

We meditate upon the Power that destroys all delusions of hunger; may she, who is abundant in her birth, impel our intellects toward the Self—she whose essence is the *praṇava* and the *śiras*, *huṃ phaṭ svāhā*.
Thus, the wise man becomes one who has accomplished his purpose and attains the same world as Sāvitrī herself.
"Victory!"—thus ends the Upaniṣad.
Oṃ! May my limbs, speech, breath, sight, hearing, and likewise strength and all my senses swell with vigor. May everything be the Upaniṣad of Brahman;
may I not reject Brahman, and may Brahman not reject me. May there be no rejection; may there be for me non-rejection.
Whatever dharmas are contained in the Upanishads for one intent upon the Self—may those be in me; may they be in me.
